newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF directors want public sale - newspapers.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF directors want public sale - newspapers.

text.p: A Thomson-CSF executive committee wrote to Prime Minister Alain Juppe on Monday to ask him to proceed with a public sale of the state-owned defence group, newspapers Les Echos and Le Figaro said Thursday.
The government is due to decide on whether to sell its 58-percent stake in the company by a market float or a private placement.
The papers said the committee ruled out the risk of a hostile takeover bid on grounds that the government does not risk losing control as it can remain a Thomson shareholder.
"If it wishes to, the state can play an active part in a privatised Thomson's board. By keeping ten percent of the capital, it would be the main shareholder", the letter says.
The Thomson executives see a three-month period before a public sale can be implemented.
Le Figaro added that a second stage could be the search for French partners to act as a hub in a planned French defence industry restructuring.
